## TB-681 ΓÇö Azure OpenAI prompt-cache prefix ordering (P1)

**Closed (2026-07-08):** Static-first user prompt assembly via `AgentUserPromptComposer` / `AgentUserPromptStaticPrefix`; quad handlers delegate to composer then `TechnologyLedgerUserPromptInjection.AppendLedgerContext`; Ask and draft-intake paths use `AskUserPromptStaticPrefix`; OTel counter `archlucid_llm_cached_prompt_tokens_total` on cached prompt tokens.

**Window:** V1 ΓÇö agent execute, Ask, and draft-intake LLM prompt assembly.

**Why:** App-level response caching (`CachingAgentCompletionClient`) only helps identical repeats. Azure OpenAI automatic prompt caching discounts cached input tokens when the first ~1024 tokens of a request are stable across calls. Versioned system prompts in `ArchLucid.AgentRuntime/Prompts/*SystemPromptTemplate.cs` and cloud-provider addenda are identical across runs, but per-run evidence and retrieval blocks may precede or interleave with static content today ΓÇö reducing cache hit rate across the four parallel agent calls and sequential retries.

**Approach:**

1. Audit and refactor `AgentUserPromptBuilder.cs` and handler-specific builders so **static prefix** order is: system template ΓåÆ cloud addendum (`CloudProviderAgentPromptComposer`) ΓåÆ policy boilerplate ΓåÆ **dynamic suffix**: evidence, retrieval hits, request-specific fields.
2. Apply the same static-first rule to `AskService` and `DraftIntakeReasoningService` user-message assembly where feasible.
3. Add OTel counters or span attributes for provider-reported cached input tokens when Azure OpenAI returns them (alongside existing `LlmCompletionAccountingClient` totals).
4. Document prefix contract in `docs/library/CONFIGURATION_REFERENCE.md` or ADR addendum ΓÇö no change to agent output schemas or gate semantics.

**Acceptance:**

- Integration or unit test asserts static system hash appears before first evidence/retrieval token in assembled user prompts for at least Topology and Compliance handlers.
- Real-mode smoke (or documented manual check) shows non-zero cached input tokens on second agent call in the same run when deployment supports prompt caching.
- No regression in `AgentPromptRegressionTests` baselines.

**Affected files:** `ArchLucid.AgentRuntime/AgentUserPromptBuilder.cs`, `TopologyAgentHandler.cs`, `ComplianceAgentHandler.cs`, `CostAgentHandler.cs`, `CriticAgentHandler.cs`, `ArchLucid.Host.Core/AskService.cs`, `LlmCompletionAccountingClient.cs`, `ArchLucid.Core/Diagnostics/ArchLucidInstrumentation.cs`.

**Refs:** **TB-179** (multi-model tiers); ADR 0005 (LLM completion pipeline); `docs/library/AI_LEVERAGE_ROADMAP.md`.

**Size estimate:** S.

## TB-682 ΓÇö Escalation-based model-tier auto-retry (P1) ΓÇö **Done** (2026-07-08)

**Closed:** `ArchitectureRunExecuteOrchestrator` quality-gate auto-retry clones the rejected agent task with an escalated `ModelTierOverride` (EconomyΓåÆStandardΓåÆPremium) when `ArchLucid:AgentOutput:QualityGate:EscalateTierOnRetry` is true (default). Helpers: `AgentModelTierEscalation`, `AgentModelTierRetryDefaults`. Tests: `AgentModelTierEscalationTests`, `ArchitectureRunExecuteOrchestratorQualityGateTierEscalationTests`.

**Window:** V1 ΓÇö `ArchitectureRunExecuteOrchestrator` quality-gate auto-retry path.

**Why:** `AgentModelTierDefaults` statically pins Compliance/Critic to Premium and Topology/Cost to Economy. Quality-gate auto-retry (`MaxAutoRetries`) re-invokes the same tier, wasting Premium spend on easy runs and failing hard runs that might succeed one tier up. Escalation routing captures the **AI_LEVERAGE_ROADMAP** 30ΓÇô50% multi-model cost target without sacrificing quality ΓÇö the gate remains the arbiter.

**Approach:**

1. Extend auto-retry in `ArchitectureRunExecuteOrchestrator.cs` (or `RealAgentExecutor` retry wrapper) to bump `LlmModelTier` one step per rejection: Economy ΓåÆ Standard ΓåÆ Premium (stop at Premium).
2. Record escalated tier and retry reason on `AgentExecutionTrace` / forensics DTO for operator visibility.

## TB-691 ΓÇö Fix Next 16 First Load JS bundle regression gate (P0)

**Status:** **Done** (2026-07-07) ΓÇö `first-load-js-baseline.mjs` reads Next 16 `.next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json` (`firstLoadUncompressedJsBytes` ΓåÆ kB); removed silent skip on Next 16 build logs; legacy Next 15 console parsing retained; fixture + Vitest coverage; `ui-static-quality` runs `npm run check:first-load-js` after `npm run build`; baseline notes updated (refresh with `npm run write:first-load-js-baseline` after intentional bundle changes).

**Window:** V1 ΓÇö restores an existing, already-relied-upon CI gate; not new scope.

**Why:** **TB-573** shipped `npm run check:first-load-js` against a committed `performance/first-load-js-baseline.v1.json` captured on **Next 15**. After the Next 16 upgrade (Turbopack default), production build output no longer prints per-route First Load JS in the format the checker parses, so the gate either silently skips or always passes regardless of real bundle size. This means every bundle-size regression since the Next 16 upgrade has gone undetected ΓÇö the CI signal the team believes exists does not exist. Found during a 2026-07-07 UI performance review while trying to trust the committed baseline numbers (`/reviews/[runId]` at 421 kB) against current code.

**Approach:**

1. Confirm the exact failure mode: run `npm run build` locally and diff actual output against what `check:first-load-js` expects to parse; capture whether it throws, skips, or false-passes.
2. Switch measurement source to `next build --experimental-build-mode=... ` route manifest or `ANALYZE=1 npm run build:analyze` stats JSON (webpack/turbopack stats are stable across Next versions) instead of parsing human-readable build console output.
3. Recapture the baseline for every route in `first-load-js-baseline.v1.json` on current Next 16 code; keep the existing ┬▒25 kB regression tolerance unless data suggests otherwise.
4. Add a fast-fail unit test asserting the parser recognizes at least N routes from a fixture build output, so a future Next upgrade breaking the format again fails loudly instead of silently.
5. Re-verify the CI workflow step actually fails the build on a synthetic regression (temporarily bloat a route, confirm gate fires, revert).

**Acceptance:**

- `check:first-load-js` demonstrably fails CI when a route's First Load JS regresses beyond tolerance on current Next 16 build output.
- Baseline file regenerated with current numbers and a comment noting the Next version it was captured on.
- Parser has a regression test using a Next 16 build-output fixture.

**Affected files:** `scripts/ci/check-first-load-js.*` (or equivalent), `performance/first-load-js-baseline.v1.json`, `archlucid-ui/next.config.ts`, CI workflow invoking the check.

**Refs:** **TB-573** (original gate), **TB-565** (`optimizePackageImports`).

**Size estimate:** S.

## TB-695 ΓÇö Migrate `useGovernanceFindingsQuery` to TanStack Query + cap fallback fan-out (P2)

**Approach:**

1. Wrap the existing fetch logic in a `useQuery` with a scoped key (tenant/workspace), matching the stale/GC-time conventions in `operator-query-stale-time.ts`.
2. Cap the fallback path's parallel `getRunExplanationSummary` fan-out (e.g. bounded batches via `Promise.all` in chunks, or a concurrency limiter already used elsewhere in the codebase per **TB-586**'s bounded-parallel pattern).
3. Confirm the primary register-fetch path's existing `Promise.all` parallelism is preserved, not regressed, by the migration.
4. Add a test asserting the fallback path never issues more than the capped number of concurrent summary requests.

**Acceptance:**

- Governance findings query participates in TanStack Query cache/dedupe like other migrated hooks.
- Fallback fan-out is provably bounded under test.
- No behavior regression for tenants on the primary (non-fallback) path.

**Affected files:** `use-governance-findings-query.ts`, `operator-query-stale-time.ts` (key/stale-time reuse).

What remains eagerly bundled/mounted is still paid by every operator page regardless of whether that page needs tours, wizards, or heavier providers.

**Approach:**

1. Use `build:analyze` (post-**TB-691** fix) to identify which pieces of `AppShellClient`'s current import graph are not yet `dynamic()` and are not needed on first paint for a representative lightweight page (e.g. `/settings/*`).

## TB-729 ΓÇö UI Container App autoscaling headroom (no Front Door change) (P1)

**Status:** **Done** (2026-07-11) ΓÇö UI Container App defaults raised to **`ui_max_replicas = 6`** and **`ui_scale_concurrent_requests = 10`** in `infra/terraform-container-apps/variables.tf`, wired through `main.tf` HTTP scale rules; documented in `README.md` and `production.tfvars.example`. No Front Door or second-origin changes.

**Window:** V1 ΓÇö solo-founder-safe traffic isolation without a deployment split.

**Why:** `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` ┬º4 ΓÇö a public marketing traffic burst (for
example a LinkedIn post or press mention) currently shares the same Container App replica pool as
authenticated operator traffic. The topology doc's "Option B" (second Container App + second Front
Door origin) would isolate this, but the owner directed avoiding new Front Door investment for
this pass. Azure Container Apps already supports HTTP-concurrency-based autoscaling independent of
Front Door; the fix is to give the existing single UI Container App more scale-out headroom, not to
add a second origin.

**Approach:**

1. In `infra/terraform-container-apps`, locate the UI Container App resource's `template` block
   (`azurerm_container_app` ΓÇö standard schema: `min_replicas`, `max_replicas`, and any `http`
   `scale_rule` with a `concurrent_requests` threshold).
2. Confirm the current `max_replicas` value and HTTP scale-rule concurrency threshold; raise
   `max_replicas` and/or lower the concurrency threshold so a traffic spike triggers additional
   replicas before requests queue.
3. Keep `min_replicas` unchanged unless cold-start latency during bursts is also a concern ΓÇö this
   item is about ceiling headroom, not baseline cost.
4. Do not add, modify, or reference `marketing_backend_hostname`, a second Container App, or any
   `infra/terraform-edge` resource as part of this item ΓÇö that is explicitly deferred (see
   **TB-731**).
5. Validate the change with a `terraform plan` against the affected root only; no application code
   changes are required.

**Acceptance:**

- UI Container App can scale to a higher replica ceiling under sustained concurrent load without
  any Front Door/DNS/origin changes.
- No new Azure resource type introduced; the app topology (one image, one Container App, one Front
  Door profile) is unchanged.
- `infra/terraform-container-apps` plan is clean (no unrelated drift) before and after the change.

**Affected files:** `infra/terraform-container-apps/*.tf` (UI Container App `template`/scale-rule
block and its `.tfvars` defaults, if the values are variablized).

**Refs:** `docs/library/PUBLIC_MARKETING_SITE_TOPOLOGY.md` (Option B, deferred),
`MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` ┬º4, ┬º6.

**Size estimate:** S.

## TB-730 ΓÇö Harden `OperatorRoleGate` / `OperatorHomeGate` against pre-redirect shell exposure (P1)

**Status:** **Done** (2026-07-11) ΓÇö `unsignedJwtSessionBlocksOperatorShell` extends deferral beyond `/` to every operator route; `OperatorRoleGate` redirects unsigned JWT sessions to `/welcome`; Vitest coverage in `operator-shell-access-gate.test.ts` and `OperatorRoleGate.test.tsx`.

**Window:** V1 ΓÇö closes the actual "buyer sees admin UI" risk identified during the
marketing/product separation assessment.

**Why:** `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` ┬º3 ΓÇö `OperatorRoleGate`
(`archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorRoleGate.tsx`) and `OperatorHomeGate`
(`archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorHomeGate.tsx`) are client components that redirect **after**
hydration and authority resolution (`useOperatorNavAuthority()`), not before render. An anonymous
or unauthorized visitor who deep-links into an operator route can see `AppShellClient` shell chrome
(sidebar, topbar) render for a frame before the `router.replace("/403")` (or marketing redirect)
takes effect. This is the real mechanism behind the "public buyers do not see product-admin UI
artifacts" acceptance criterion ΓÇö a marketing/product deployment split would not fix it, since the
leak is internal to the operator app's own render path.

**Approach:**

1. In `OperatorRoleGate.tsx`, change the render branch so that while `isAuthorityLoading` is true,
   or before the first authority resolution completes, the component renders a neutral loading
   state (blank/skeleton with no sidebar/topbar content) instead of falling through to
   `<>{children}</>` ΓÇö currently the final `return <>{children}</>;` fires whenever the redirect
   condition is false, which includes the loading window.
2. Apply the same principle to `OperatorHomeGate.tsx` for the `/` route.
3. Confirm `AppShellClient` does not render `SidebarNav`/`OperatorShellTopBar` content until the
   gate has resolved ΓÇö the neutral loading state should replace the whole shell frame, not just the
   page body, so no nav labels/branding specific to the product are visible pre-resolution.
4. Add/extend tests (`OperatorRoleGate.test.tsx` already exists) asserting that no sidebar/topbar
   text or nav items are present in the DOM during the loading window for an anonymous session,
   only after resolution.
5. This is a UI-only change; no backend/API contract changes.

**Acceptance:**

- An anonymous visitor deep-linking to any `(operator)` route sees a neutral loading state, never
  sidebar/nav/product-shell content, until authority resolves and either renders the page or
  redirects.
- Existing authorized-user flows render with no added perceptible delay beyond the existing
  authority-resolution round trip.
- `OperatorRoleGate.test.tsx` (and an equivalent for `OperatorHomeGate` if not already covered)
  assert the no-premature-shell-content behavior.

**Affected files:** `archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorRoleGate.tsx`,
`archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorHomeGate.tsx`, `archlucid-ui/src/components/AppShellClient.tsx`,
`archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorRoleGate.test.tsx`.

**Refs:** `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` ┬º3, ┬º6, ┬º8.

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-731 — Instrument the marketing/product re-split trigger metric (P2) — **Done** (2026-07-17)

**Window:** V1 — makes the future "revisit Option B / real domain split" decision data-driven
instead of calendar-driven.

**Shipped:** `infra/terraform-monitoring/marketing_product_resplit_triggers.tf` (UI `CpuPercentage` 15m + `Replicas` 15m metric alerts); Prometheus signup daily/hourly rules in `prometheus_slo_rules.tf`; optional `first_tenant_funnel_workbook` module; variables/outputs/checks; `infra/prometheus/archlucid-alerts.yml` mirror; concrete threshold table in `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` §6. No Front Door or UI app code changes — signup events already emitted via `recordFirstTenantFunnelEvent("signup")`.

**Why:** `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` §6 recommends deferring any
deployment/domain split until a concrete trigger fires, but no such trigger is currently measured.
Without instrumentation, the decision to eventually split (which does require Front Door
investment) has no signal to act on.

**Approach:**

1. Identify the cheapest existing signal that already indicates traffic pressure on the shared UI
   Container App ΓÇö Container App CPU/replica-count metrics (already emitted to whichever
   monitoring stack `infra/terraform-monitoring` wires up) are the primary candidate; do not
   introduce a new telemetry vendor.
2. Add a threshold-based alert (or dashboard panel, if alerting infrastructure is not yet in place)
   for sustained high replica count / CPU saturation on the UI Container App during a traffic burst.
3. Separately, add a simple counter/dimension on self-serve signup volume (reusing the existing
   `recordFirstTenantFunnelEvent` / first-tenant funnel diagnostics already emitted from
   `SignupForm.tsx`) so growth in that funnel is visible without a new analytics system.
4. Document both trigger conditions (traffic-pressure threshold and signup-volume threshold)
   directly in `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` ┬º6 once the concrete threshold values
   are chosen, so the next assessment pass has an explicit go/no-go signal instead of re-deriving
   one.
5. This item does not implement Option B or any Front Door change ΓÇö it only instruments the signal
   that would justify picking that item up later.

**Acceptance:**

- A Container App CPU/replica-saturation signal is visible in the existing monitoring stack with a
  defined threshold.
- Self-serve signup volume is visible via existing first-tenant funnel diagnostics, with no new
  third-party analytics tool introduced.
- `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` ┬º6 is updated with the chosen concrete threshold
  values once set.

**Affected files:** `infra/terraform-monitoring/*.tf` (alert rule),
`docs/library/MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` (┬º6 threshold values), no `archlucid-ui`
application code changes expected beyond confirming existing funnel event emission is sufficient.

**Refs:** `MARKETING_PRODUCT_SEPARATION_ASSESSMENT.md` ┬º4, ┬º6; `docs/library/PUBLIC_MARKETING_SITE_TOPOLOGY.md`
(Option B, the deferred lever this trigger would justify revisiting).

**Size estimate:** S.

its "contextual help," conflating a short in-line answer with long-form documentation. The
taxonomy calls for a page-scoped answer to exactly four questions (what is this page / what should
I do next / why is this state empty / where do I configure the prerequisite), not a jump to a
long article.

**Approach:**

1. Add `archlucid-ui/src/lib/contextual-help-registry.ts`, keyed the same way as
   `page-help-topic-map.ts`, with up to four short fields per page (Γëñ ~120 words total); reuse
   `ContextualHelp.tsx` / `FieldHelpTooltip.tsx` / `ui/tooltip.tsx` shapes rather than inventing new
   popover chrome.

   `TB-` roadmap label.

   back to today's `/help` deep link otherwise, so migration can land incrementally.
4. Write the four-question copy for the starting page set: `/reviews` (empty state),
   `/governance/findings`, `/digests`, `/planning`, `/advisory`, `/value-report`.

**Acceptance:**

- The six starting pages show in-line short answers instead of a raw jump to a full article.
- No contextual-help field exceeds the length/content constraints; pages not yet migrated are
  unaffected (fallback path).

**Affected files:** `archlucid-ui/src/lib/contextual-help-registry.ts` (new),

## TB-754 — Verify CD post-deploy retry repo vars (P2) — **Done** (2026-07-17)

**Window:** V1.

**Source:** Owner cold-start Q&A 2026-07-12 — free Azure-bill levers only.

**Shipped:** `scripts/ci/verify-cd-post-deploy-retry-vars.ps1` (audit exit 0/1/2, `-Apply` sets recommended `6`/`10`); cold-start checklist in [`GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md`](../operations/GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md) and [`DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md`](DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md) (documents `cd.yml` fallback **6** vs local bash default **1**); `bootstrap-github-cd-environments.ps1` re-runs verify after bootstrap.

**Problem:** New Container App revisions often fail the first smoke/`deployment-evidence` pass while DbUp and process start complete. `scripts/ci/bootstrap-github-cd-environments.ps1` sets `CD_POST_DEPLOY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=6` and `CD_POST_DEPLOY_RETRY_WAIT_SECONDS=10`, but environments bootstrapped earlier (or manually) may still use the workflow default of **1** attempt — false smoke failures and operator panic during routine cold starts.

**Scope:**

1. Audit GitHub repo/environment variables for every CD target (`dev` / `staging` / `production`) and set retries to the bootstrap defaults unless intentionally lower.
2. Document expected values in [`GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md`](../operations/GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md) + [`DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md`](DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md) as a one-line "cold start" checklist item.
3. Optional: note in `archlucid stack doctor` / CD preflight that missing retry vars are a warn.

**Explicitly out of scope:** Raising `*_min_replicas`, CPU/memory, Redis, ReadyToRun/Debian, migration-out-of-process Jobs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Staging and production smoke jobs retry through cold start without changing Azure Container Apps SKUs.
- Docs state the expected repo var values and that they do not increase Azure compute spend.

**Affected files:** `docs/operations/GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md`, `docs/library/DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md`, optionally `scripts/ci/bootstrap-github-cd-environments.ps1` (already sets vars ΓÇö verify only).

**Cross-ref:** **TB-755**, **TB-759**, **TB-657**.

**Size estimate:** XS.

## TB-755 — Enable CD canary + bake (staging/production) (P2) — **Done** (2026-07-17)

**Window:** V1.

**Source:** Owner cold-start Q&A 2026-07-12 — free Azure-bill levers only.

**Shipped:** `api_revision_mode = "Multiple"` in `staging.tfvars.example` and `production.tfvars.example`; `scripts/ci/verify-cd-canary-vars.ps1` (audit/`-Apply` for `CD_CANARY_ENABLED=true`, `CD_CANARY_INITIAL_PERCENT=10`, `CD_CANARY_BAKE_MINUTES=3`); bootstrap sets canary vars and re-verifies; canary checklist in [`GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md`](../operations/GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md), [`DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md`](DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md), and [`PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`](../runbooks/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md#part-c--canary-promotion-container-apps). Existing `cd.yml` split/bake/promote + smoke gate unchanged.

**Problem:** CD can pin 100% traffic to a brand-new revision immediately. Users then hit DbUp/JIT/SQL connect latency. Canary + bake already exist in `.github/workflows/cd.yml` and [`PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`](../runbooks/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md#part-c--canary-promotion-container-apps) but default off.

**Scope:**

1. Set Terraform `api_revision_mode = "Multiple"` for staging/production (apply once).
2. Set repo vars: `CD_CANARY_ENABLED=true`, `CD_CANARY_INITIAL_PERCENT` (e.g. 10), `CD_CANARY_BAKE_MINUTES` (e.g. 2ΓÇô5).
3. Confirm smoke still gates promotion to 100% and rollback path still works with `CD_ROLLBACK_ON_SMOKE_FAILURE`.
4. Document operator expectations (brief dual-revision overlap is normal; not a `min_replicas` increase).

**Explicitly out of scope:** Raising replica floors; worker/UI canary unless API path proves useful first.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Staging (then production) deploys split traffic, bake, smoke, then promote.
- No change to `api_min_replicas` / `ui_min_replicas` / `worker_min_replicas`.

**Affected files:** `infra/terraform-container-apps/*.tfvars` (or env secrets), GitHub repo vars, `docs/runbooks/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/operations/GITHUB_CD_ENVIRONMENTS.md`.

**Cross-ref:** **TB-754**, **TB-657**, **TB-759**.

**Window:** V1.

**Source:** Owner cold-start Q&A 2026-07-12 — free Azure-bill levers only.

**Shipped:** "When to skip full CD" table in [`DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md`](DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md); unnecessary-rerun guidance in [`DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md`](DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md); informational `::notice` in `.github/workflows/cd.yml` when the active API revision already runs the build digest (does not block deploy).

2. Clarify that CD already uses digest + revision-suffix for intentional rolls ΓÇö do not add extra manual updates "to be safe."
3. Optional: CD step summary note when image digest matches previous active revision (informational; do not block intentional force-roll).

**Explicitly out of scope:** Changing CD concurrency or image tagging scheme; Terraform lifecycle (already `ignore_changes` on image ΓÇö **TB-657**).

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Operators have a written rule for skip vs deploy.
- No new always-on Azure capacity.

## TB-757 ΓÇö UI proxy / client warm-up tolerance (P2)

**Window:** V1.

**Source:** Owner cold-start Q&A 2026-07-12 ΓÇö free Azure-bill levers only.

**Problem:** During a new API revision's first seconds (or while readiness is still catching up), the UI BFF (`/api/proxy/*`) can return **502 Upstream API unreachable**. Clients may toast immediately (**TB-157** correctly labels API unreachable) even though a short retry would succeed ΓÇö noisy UX after deploys without buying more replicas.

**Scope:**

1. Add a **bounded** client and/or proxy retry (e.g. 1ΓÇô2 retries with short backoff) for idempotent GETs on 502/503/upstream-unreachable only ΓÇö do not mask lasting outages.
2. Optionally defer first toast until retries exhaust (keep **TB-157** copy).
3. Do **not** raise `PROXY_UPSTREAM_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (already 60s) as the primary fix ΓÇö that lengthens hangs.

**Explicitly out of scope:** Azure Front Door; raising UI/API `min_replicas`; changing API readiness probes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Simulated brief 502 then 200 on a GET does not toast; sustained 502 still surfaces **ArchLucid API unreachable**.
- Unit/Vitest coverage for retry policy.
- No new Azure resources.

**Affected files:** `archlucid-ui/src/app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts`, client fetch helpers / toast policy, related tests; `docs/runbooks/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` (brief note).

**Cross-ref:** **TB-156**, **TB-157**, **TB-754**, **TB-755**.

**Size estimate:** S.

## TB-760 ΓÇö Fix help-search-catalog "First review guide" mislabeling (P0) ΓÇö **Done 2026-07-12**

**Window:** V1.

**Closure:** `first-review-guide` START_HERE topic repointed to `/help/first-hour-operator-path`; new `review-guide` topic added for `/help/review-guide`; `help-search-panel-catalog.test.ts` asserts both routes.

**Source:** [`help_review_and_architecture_guidance_assessment.md`](../architecture/help_review_and_architecture_guidance_assessment.md) ┬º2, ┬º13.1, ┬º16, ┬º18 (Step 1) ΓÇö repository-grounded IA assessment of `/help/review-guide` and adjacent review/architecture help content, 2026-07-12.

**Problem:** `archlucid-ui/src/lib/help-search-panel-catalog.ts:54-60` defines a `START_HERE_TOPICS` entry with `id: "first-review-guide"` and `title: "First review guide"`, but its `action.href` points at `/help/review-guide` (a page titled "Review guide" on arrival) instead of `/help/first-hour-operator-path` (the page actually titled "First-review guide", `product-documentation-registry.ts:76`). Any user who searches "first review" from the global help search/drawer and clicks this result lands on a page whose own `<h1>` disagrees with what they clicked ΓÇö a confirmed, shipped bug, not a hypothetical naming risk. This entry is mounted on every route where the search panel/drawer is available (global shell), independent of `/help/review-guide`'s own content quality.

**Scope:**

1. Repoint the existing `id: "first-review-guide"` entry's `action` to `{ kind: "route", href: "/help/first-hour-operator-path", helpSlug: "first-hour-operator-path" }`, keeping its existing `id`, `title`, `description`, and `keywords` unchanged.
2. Add a new, separate `START_HERE_TOPICS` entry for `/help/review-guide` itself ΓÇö `id: "review-guide"`, `title: "Review guide"`, a description reflecting its actual wizard-field-reference content (do not reuse the old description), `action: { kind: "route", href: "/help/review-guide", helpSlug: "review-guide" }`.
3. Update or add the corresponding test in `archlucid-ui/src/lib/help-search-panel-catalog.test.ts` asserting both entries resolve to their correct, distinct routes.

**Explicitly out of scope:** Any other topic in `help-search-panel-catalog.ts`; any other help route; `/help/review-guide`'s or `/help/first-hour-operator-path`'s own page content (see **TB-764**, out of scope here).

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Searching "first review" from the global help search/drawer and opening the top result lands on `/help/first-hour-operator-path`, whose own heading matches the search-result title.
- A distinct "Review guide" search entry exists and resolves to `/help/review-guide`.
- `help-search-panel-catalog.test.ts` asserts both routes.

**Affected files:** `archlucid-ui/src/lib/help-search-panel-catalog.ts`, `archlucid-ui/src/lib/help-search-panel-catalog.test.ts`.

**Owner decision (2026-07-12):** **Path 2** ΓÇö [`PENDING_QUESTIONS.md`](../PENDING_QUESTIONS.md) *Resolved 2026-07-12 (PQ-HELP-01 ΓÇö TB-761 Path 2)*. Cleared to implement.

**Problem:** `/help/evidence-intake` ("Start a review") and `/help/review-packages` ("Review packages") both resolve to the same source file, `docs/library/customer-facing/WORKFLOW_RECIPES_BY_PERSONA.md` (`product-documentation-registry.ts:140-152`) ΓÇö byte-identical rendered content under two different titles and summaries, both featured in the `/help` landing grid (`HELP_CENTER_FEATURED_SLUGS`). Neither page's title or summary describes what a visitor actually receives (four persona API/CLI recipes for architects, governance leads, procurement reviewers, and platform engineers). This is the assessment's single most damaging finding: it means two of the four pages `/help/review-guide`'s own "Related guides" section points to are indistinguishable from each other.

**Scope (Path 2):**

1. Relocate persona API/CLI recipes out of buyer/operator `/help` ΓÇö keep `WORKFLOW_RECIPES_BY_PERSONA.md` (or successor) as integration/engineering documentation; do **not** feature it as product-help Guides (optional later Documentation exposure via **TB-734**).
2. Rewrite `/help/evidence-intake` to cover evidence formats, what "verifying intake" means, and how the quick-start / guided-intake / templates-and-imports path switcher (`ReviewsNewPathSwitcher`) differs ΓÇö the content `WizardEvidenceUploadZone`'s existing "View the start review guide" link already promises.
3. Rewrite `/help/review-packages` so its content matches its title (browsing/inspecting/exporting packages), which does not exist anywhere in the help corpus today.
4. Update `product-documentation-registry.ts` entries (and `HELP_CENTER_FEATURED_SLUGS` if the page count changes) so the two slugs no longer share a `sourcePaths` value.

**Explicitly out of scope:** The terminology decision between "review package" and "architecture package" (Unresolved owner decision #1 in the assessment) ΓÇö do not resolve implicitly while doing this rewrite; whichever noun is later chosen applies to both paths equally.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- `/help/evidence-intake` and `/help/review-packages` render distinct content, each matching its own title and summary.
- No registry entry shares a `sourcePaths` value with another entry in a way that produces duplicate rendered pages.
- Persona API/CLI recipe content is preserved as integration/engineering documentation ΓÇö not deleted outright and not featured as buyer product-help Guides.

**Affected files:** `archlucid-ui/src/lib/product-documentation-registry.ts`, `docs/library/customer-facing/WORKFLOW_RECIPES_BY_PERSONA.md`, new buyer-safe markdown sources for both help slugs, `archlucid-ui/src/lib/help-center-catalog.ts` (featured-grid membership), possibly `product-documentation-content-kinds.ts`.

**Cross-ref:** **TB-764** (review-guide's "Finalize the review package" section links here), **TB-732ΓÇô737** (IA taxonomy cluster, `contentKind` metadata applies to any relocated content).

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-781 — Organization-Private policy pack distribution scope (P1)

**Window:** V1 (private beta).

**Status:** **Done** (2026-07-15 — `PolicyPackDistributionScope` + rules/guards, migration **276**, UI Organization private badge, catalog promote blocked for OrganizationPrivate packs, trust copy in `DEFAULT_POLICY_PACKS_V1.md`).

**Source:** Owner evaluation of OpenAI product feedback (2026-07-15) — gap between designed policy-pack capabilities (bundled packs, assignment/precedence, required vs optional, versioning, no marketplace) and a first-class **Organization Private** distribution classification. Aligns with ArchLucid philosophy: institutional knowledge remains the customer’s asset.

**Why:** Customer-authored packs already exist (`TenantCustom` / `WorkspaceCustom` / `ProjectCustom`) and are tenant-scoped, but that privacy is an *emergent* property of tenancy — not a buyer-named, irrevocable product contract. Fortune 100 private-beta buyers need a named property they can point to: Organization Private packs are not published, not discoverable outside the tenant, and not used to train or improve anyone else’s packs. Without an explicit `DistributionScope`, a future Marketplace / Org Shared feature has no sealed default.

**Keep two axes (do not collapse):**

| Axis | Answers | Existing / proposed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Origin** (`PackType`) | Who authored it? | `BuiltIn`, `PlatformDefault`, `TenantCustom`, `WorkspaceCustom`, `ProjectCustom` — **unchanged** |
| **Distribution** (`DistributionScope`) | Who may see / install it? | **V1:** `Platform` (built-in / platform default), `OrganizationPrivate`. **Reserved (unimplemented):** `OrganizationShared`, `Marketplace` |

**In scope (V1 minimal):**

1. **Model:** Add `DistributionScope` string (or enum-backed string constants class) on `PolicyPack` + DDL column on `dbo.PolicyPacks` (single unified schema file). Seed/create rules:
   - `BuiltIn` / `PlatformDefault` → `Platform`
   - `TenantCustom` / `WorkspaceCustom` / `ProjectCustom` → `OrganizationPrivate` (default; immutable for V1 — no API to widen to Shared/Marketplace)
2. **API / DTO:** Surface `distributionScope` on pack list/detail responses; reject any request that attempts to set Shared/Marketplace or to change away from OrganizationPrivate on customer packs.
3. **Hard deny (future-proof):** Central guard that OrganizationPrivate packs cannot enter any cross-tenant catalog, marketplace listing, or “share with other tenants” path. Today that path may not exist — still ship the guard + unit tests so it cannot be added without failing tests.
4. **Do not confuse with in-tenant versioning:** `PublishVersion` / SemVer content revision **within the owning tenant** remains allowed. OrganizationPrivate blocks *distribution outside the tenant*, not pack lifecycle inside it.
5. **UI:** Buyer-visible **Organization private** badge (or StatusTag) on My packs / pack detail for custom packs; short helper copy that packs never leave the organization.
6. **Trust / GTM copy:** One trust-center / security-trust sentence + optional help note distinguishing **Review Engine Knowledge** (ArchLucid-built-in expertise) vs **Organization Knowledge** (customer policy packs / institutional standards). Claim language must be defensible: no training on OrganizationPrivate pack content for other customers’ packs; no cross-tenant discoverability.
7. **Tests:** Create custom pack → scope is OrganizationPrivate; cannot widen; Platform packs are Platform; regression that no publish-to-shared-catalog seam exists for OrganizationPrivate.

**Non-goals (explicit):**

- Organization Shared (multi-tenant company holdings) — reserve enum value only.
- Marketplace / public discoverability — reserve enum value only; no UI, no APIs.
- Replacing or renaming `PackType`.
- Customer-managed keys / cryptographic pack encryption (out of scope unless owner promotes).
- Changing assignment precedence, required vs optional, or bundled pack seeding behavior.
- Professional-services IP tiers (Customer-exclusive vs ArchLucid-owned) in marketing SOW — related narrative only; not this model change.

**Approach:**

1. Add `PolicyPackDistributionScope` constants + property on `PolicyPack`; migrate `ArchLucid.sql` / `ArchLucid_Unified_Schema.sql` (and forward migration if the repo uses numbered migrations for this table).
2. Set scope in `PolicyPackManagementService.CreatePackAsync` and default-pack seeder; backfill existing custom packs to OrganizationPrivate / platform packs to Platform.
3. Enforce immutability + Shared/Marketplace reject in validators / management service.
4. Expose on OpenAPI + UI badge on `/governance/policy-packs`.
5. Add trust-center / `DEFAULT_POLICY_PACKS_V1.md` (or security-trust) one-paragraph buyer claim; Vitest/doc guard if other trust claims are already guarded that way.
6. Unit + API tests for defaults, immutability, and “no cross-tenant publish” seam.

**Acceptance:**

- Every pack has an explicit `DistributionScope`; customer-authored packs are OrganizationPrivate and cannot be widened via API.
- Operators see an Organization private label on custom packs without reading engineer `PackType` names.
- Buyer-facing trust copy can honestly say Organization Private packs are not published, not discoverable outside the tenant, and not used to train/improve other customers’ packs (with legal/ops alignment noted in PR if claim wording is tightened).
- `OrganizationShared` and `Marketplace` exist only as reserved constants — no implementation paths.
- In-tenant `PublishVersion` for custom packs still works.

**Affected files (expected):**

- `ArchLucid.Contracts/Governance/PolicyPacks/PolicyPack.cs`, new `PolicyPackDistributionScope.cs`
- `ArchLucid.Persistence/Scripts/ArchLucid.sql` (+ unified schema twin)
- `ArchLucid.Decisioning/Governance/PolicyPacks/PolicyPackManagementService.cs` (+ validators / DTOs / OpenAPI)
- `ArchLucid.Persistence/Governance/*PolicyPack*` repositories/mappers
- `archlucid-ui` policy-packs list/detail (`PolicyPacksRegisteredListSection`, detail clients)
- Trust / GTM: `docs/go-to-market/DEFAULT_POLICY_PACKS_V1.md` and/or operator security-trust surface
- Tests: `PolicyPackManagementServiceTests`, API integration tests, UI Vitest for badge copy

**Refs:** `PolicyPackType`, tenant isolation (**TB-071** cluster / INV-001), marketing Customer-exclusive PS copy (`MarketingCustomPolicyPackAuthoringSection`), deferred marketplace stance.

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-782 — Report Problem V1 scope contract (P1)

**Window:** V1 (private beta).

**Status:** Done (2026-07-15) — `docs/library/REPORT_PROBLEM_V1_SCOPE.md`; `archlucid-ui/src/lib/report-problem-surfaces.ts` registry; `report-problem-copy.ts` SLA/consent constants; Vitest drift guards; `docs/engineering/AGENTS.md` pointer.

**Source:** OpenAI private-beta trust discussion (2026-07-15) + scoped engineering review. Guiding principle: *customers can forgive defects; they rarely forgive feeling ignored.*

**Why:** ArchLucid already surfaces copyable correlation/request IDs (**TB-271** Done) and redacted support bundles (**TB-628** Done), but the operator path still ends in manual mailto assembly. A productized **Report Problem** action must be deliberately scoped so it increases trust without noise, consent fatigue, or compliance risk from silent log exfiltration.

**In scope (V1 contract artifact):**

1. Publish `docs/library/REPORT_PROBLEM_V1_SCOPE.md` (or equivalent) defining:
   - **High-stakes surfaces only** — review run failure, commit/export failure, auth/session break, unexpected empty/broken core pages (`/reviews`, `/reviews/[runId]`, executive summary load fail, governance queue hard fail). **Not** every 400, validation toast, or empty list.
   - **Captured fields (with consent):** review id (when in context), workspace id, tenant id, product/API+UI version, browser/client user-agent summary, correlation id and/or client request id, route, error code/title, optional operator note.
   - **Explicit non-capture:** raw client log scrape, prompts, evidence bodies, secrets, mailbox PII beyond submitter identity already known from auth.
   - **Diagnostics posture:** optional **redacted support bundle** attach only (**TB-787**); never auto-attach.
   - **SLA copy (owner 2026-07-15):** “We received your report (reference **{id}**). We’ll respond by the **next business day**.” Same string in UI + email ack (**TB-789**).
2. Add `archlucid-ui/src/lib/report-problem-surfaces.ts` registry enumerating component paths / route patterns allowed to render Report Problem (Vitest drift guard in **TB-791**).
3. Add shared copy constants in `archlucid-ui/src/lib/report-problem-copy.ts` (SLA, consent label, field glossary).

**Non-goals:**

- Report Problem on every error surface.
- In-product chat or implied sub-hour SLA.
- Third-party ticketing CRM sync (Jira/ServiceNow/Zendesk) — defer V1.1 unless owner promotes.
- Replacing `/settings/support` manual bundle download workflow.

**Acceptance:**

- Contract doc is linked from **TB-790** help topic and engineering `AGENTS.md` pointer.
- Registry lists initial high-stakes surfaces and is importable by UI + tests.
- SLA + consent strings exist in one module (no ad hoc duplicates).

**Size estimate:** XS.

## TB-788 — Support problem-report intake API (P1)

**Window:** V1.

**Status:** Done (2026-07-16) — `POST /v1/support/problem-reports` (`SupportProblemReportsController`, `ExecuteAuthority`); migration **278** `dbo.SupportProblemReports`; `SupportProblemReportIntakeService` + `SupportProblemReportNotifier` (`Email:SupportInbox`); UI `report-problem-intake-api.ts`; `SupportProblemReportEndpointTests` + application/persistence unit tests.

**Problem:** Structured reports need a durable server-side intake with a reference id support can quote — not only a `mailto:` query string.

1. Add `POST /v1/support/problem-reports` (`ExecuteAuthority` or `ReadAuthority` + tenant scope — prefer **ExecuteAuthority** to match support bundle posture).
2. Request body: `ReportProblemContext` DTO + `operatorNote` + `consentGranted` + optional `attachSupportBundle` flag.
3. Response `202 Accepted`: `{ referenceId, submittedAtUtc, slaMessage }` where `referenceId` is a new GUID (display label **Report reference**).
4. Persist row in `dbo.SupportProblemReports` (single DDL file): tenant/workspace scope, actor user id, context JSON (redacted envelope), note, correlation/request ids, bundle blob path if attached, status `Open`.
5. Emit audit event `SupportProblemReportSubmitted` (no evidence bodies).
6. Hook notification: email to `ARCHLUCID_SUPPORT_EMAIL` distribution + optional Teams/internal webhook (implementation choice in PR; minimum = email).
7. API + integration tests: creates row, returns reference id, rejects without consent.

**Acceptance:**

- Submitting from UI returns a stable `referenceId`.
- Row is tenant-scoped; cross-tenant read denied.
- Payload excludes forbidden fields per **TB-782** contract.

**TB-793 — TB-797** were added 2026-07-15 from the **private-beta access-path blocker assessment** ([`private_beta_access_prompt_07152026.md`](../assessments/private_beta_access_prompt_07152026.md); ephemeral session outputs use gitignored `docs/assessments/latest_*.md`). The assessment was deliberately scoped to only the six proofs an invited private-beta user needs — receive/use an invitation, authenticate, land in the correct tenant, reach core workflows, complete a first meaningful action, and recover from expected failures — and excluded visual polish, copy, feature requests, and IA work. It confirmed two P0s by direct code contradiction / trace, not inference: the invite UI calls a backend endpoint that does not exist anywhere in the repo (**P0-1**, split into **TB-793**–**TB-795**), and every signed-out deep link to an operator route is redirected to the marketing `/welcome` page with the target discarded (**P0-2**, **TB-796**). **TB-797** is the canonical JwtBearer smoke test that gates any private-beta invite wave and proves both fixes together end to end.

**TB-925** was added 2026-07-21 from a re-run of the same private-beta access-path assessment (ephemeral `docs/assessments/latest_beta_access_202607211939.md`). Prior invite/deep-link P0s (**TB-793**–**TB-797**) are Done; the re-run confirmed a new P0 on the **live** API process: forged `x-tenant-id` changes resolved scope and invite listing (HTTP 200) despite authenticated `tenant_id` claims, while current source documents claims-win + `ScopeIdentityBindingMiddleware` 403. **TB-925** is **Done** (2026-07-22).

**TB-927** and **TB-928** were added 2026-07-22 as the remaining private-beta access-path P0 follow-ups from the same assessment re-run after **TB-925** closed. **TB-927** closes the smoke gap where proofs 1 and 5 are only **PARTIALLY PROVEN**: today's `live-api-private-beta-access.spec.ts` creates/validates an invite but continues as an injected **admin** JWT and creates a review via API `createRun`, never walking invitee accept → `PostAuthBootstrap` session → Operator first action. **TB-928** closes deploy-time blind spots where `acceptUrl=null` (missing `EmailNotification:OperatorBaseUrl`) and invite accept → `LocalTrialJwtIssuer` session issuance (missing `Auth:Trial:LocalIdentity` PEM/issuer/audience) were listed as unconfirmed risks — surfacing them in existing auth configuration diagnostics and returning actionable errors instead of opaque 500s.

## TB-793 — Tenant-scoped user invitation admin API (P0)

**Window:** V1 (private beta).

**Status:** Done (2026-07-15) — `UsersAdminController`; `UserInvitationAdminService`; `IUserInvitationRepository` (Dapper + in-memory); migration **277** + consolidated DDL; `UsersAdminInvitationEndpointTests`.

**Source:** Private-beta access-path assessment (2026-07-15), confirmed P0-1.

**Problem:** `SettingsRolesInvitePanel.tsx` posts to `POST /v1/admin/users/invite`. No controller serves that route in any `ArchLucid.Api` project (`rg "admin/users" --type cs` and `rg "[Ii]nvite" --type cs` return zero backend matches), and the endpoint has never appeared in the OpenAPI contract (`ArchLucid.Api.Tests/Contracts/openapi-v1.contract.snapshot.json`). The invite step of the private-beta access path has no working implementation. The only real provisioning paths today are SCIM (`ScimUsersController`, works, `ScimWrite`-gated) and manual IdP role-claim assignment — neither is reachable from this UI and neither notifies the invitee.

**Approach:**

1. Add `UsersAdminController` (`ArchLucid.Api/Controllers/Admin/UsersAdminController.cs`, one class per file):
   - `POST /v1/admin/users/invite` — body `{ email, appRole, message? }`; validate RFC-parseable email and `appRole` against the `ArchLucidRoles` assignable set (Admin | Operator | Reader | Auditor, matching `SETTINGS_ROLES_ASSIGNABLE`); `[Authorize(Policy = ArchLucidPolicies.AdminAuthority)]`.
   - `GET /v1/admin/users/invitations` — list pending/expired/revoked invitations, tenant-scoped via `IScopeContextProvider` (never from request body).
   - `DELETE /v1/admin/users/invitations/{id}` — revoke.
2. Add `dbo.UserInvitations` DDL to the single existing DDL file for the operational database (`ArchLucid.Persistence/Scripts/ArchLucid.sql` and `ArchLucid_Unified_Schema.sql`, per repo convention) plus a numbered migration script: id, tenant_id, workspace_id, email, app_role, invited_by, created_at_utc, expires_at_utc (default +14 days), status (`Pending` \| `Revoked` \| `Accepted`), single-use opaque token hash.
3. Dapper repository (`IUserInvitationRepository` / `SqlUserInvitationRepository`) following existing `Sql*Repository` patterns — no ORM.
4. Idempotency: a duplicate invite to the same pending email returns the existing record (200), not a second row. An invite to an email with an existing directory user returns 409 with a problem-details body the UI can render.
5. Email delivery is explicitly **out of scope** — return the invitation record (tenant name, role, expiry) so an admin can relay it manually; do not add an email-provider dependency.

**Non-goals:**

- Invite-token redemption/sign-in flow (invitees still authenticate via the tenant IdP; the token exists to track acceptance, not to replace OIDC sign-in).
- Email delivery integration.
- Changing `ArchLucidRoles` / `ArchLucidPolicies` values.

**Acceptance:**

- Non-admin caller receives 403; unauthenticated caller receives 401.
- Invalid email returns 400; duplicate-pending invite is idempotent; invite to an existing directory user returns 409.
- Invitation rows are tenant-scoped from claims, not request body (no cross-tenant creation or listing).
- Regenerated OpenAPI contract snapshot includes the three new paths; `npm run generate:api-types` regenerates `archlucid-ui/src/lib/api-types.generated.ts` without manual edits (root workspace rule `Http-Surface-Docs-And-Clients.mdc`).

**Affected files:** `ArchLucid.Api/Controllers/Admin/UsersAdminController.cs`, new `ArchLucid.Contracts/Admin/UserInvitation*.cs` DTOs (one type per file), `ArchLucid.Persistence/Scripts/ArchLucid.sql`, `ArchLucid.Persistence/Scripts/ArchLucid_Unified_Schema.sql`, new numbered migration script, new `SqlUserInvitationRepository.cs`, `ArchLucid.Api.Tests/Contracts/openapi-v1.contract.snapshot.json`, `archlucid-ui/src/lib/api-types.generated.ts`.

**Depends on:** none (foundational for **TB-794**, **TB-795**, **TB-797**).

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-794 — Invite UI truthful failure state + pending-invitations panel (P0)

**Window:** V1 (private beta).

**Status:** Done (2026-07-15) — `SettingsRolesInvitePanel` uses `admin-user-invitations.ts` (no preview-success on 404); success toast shows TB-793 reference id; `PendingInvitationsPanel` lists/revokes via GET/DELETE invitations; `requestPrincipalAppRoleAssignment` preview path removed; Vitest guards.

**Source:** Private-beta access-path assessment (2026-07-15), confirmed P0-1.

**Problem:** `SettingsRolesInvitePanel.tsx` treats a 404/405/501 from the (currently missing) invite endpoint as success: `"Invite recorded in the UI for {email}. The invite API is not available on this environment yet."` A beta admin believes an invite went out; nothing was persisted and the invitee has no way in. `admin-role-assignment-request.ts` has the same preview-success pattern for `PUT /v1/admin/users/{id}/role`.

**Approach:**

1. In `SettingsRolesInvitePanel.tsx`, remove the `"preview"` outcome branch: a 404/405/501 must render the existing error toast (`showError`), not a success toast. Keep the directory-unavailable empty state unchanged.
2. Add a pending-invitations list to `/settings/users?tab=users` (or the roles sub-panel) sourced from **TB-793**'s `GET /v1/admin/users/invitations`, with a revoke action calling `DELETE /v1/admin/users/invitations/{id}`.
3. Re-check `requestPrincipalAppRoleAssignment` in `admin-role-assignment-request.ts` once **TB-793** lands — apply the same honest-failure fix if its backing endpoint is still absent (verify at implementation time; do not assume it is in scope here).

**Acceptance:**

- A missing/erroring invite endpoint never shows a success-styled toast.
- A successful invite shows the real reference id returned by **TB-793**.
- Pending invitations are listed and revocable from the UI.

**Affected files:** `archlucid-ui/src/app/(operator)/settings/users/_sections/SettingsRolesInvitePanel.tsx`, new `PendingInvitationsPanel.tsx`, `archlucid-ui/src/lib/admin-role-assignment-request.ts` (verify only).

**Depends on:** **TB-793**.

**Size estimate:** S.

## TB-796 — Preserve deep-link target through signed-out sign-in on operator routes (P0)

**Window:** V1 (private beta).

**Status:** Done (2026-07-15) — `OperatorRoleGate` redirects unsigned JWT sessions to `buildAuthSignInHref({ returnPath: pathname + search })` instead of `/welcome`; unsafe paths fall back to plain `/auth/signin`; `OperatorRoleGate.test.tsx` updated.

**Source:** Private-beta access-path assessment (2026-07-15), confirmed P0-2.

**Problem:** `OperatorRoleGate.tsx` redirects any signed-out visitor on a JWT-mode operator route straight to `/welcome`, discarding the pathname and query string (`storePostSignInReturnUrl` is never called on this path — its only callers are `initiateOidcRedirect` via `/auth/signin?returnUrl=` and the session-expiry flow). A beta invite/Slack link to `/reviews/{runId}` therefore lands the user on the marketing page, and after sign-in they land on `/` — not the linked resource. This fails the assessment's routing bar ("not `/welcome`, not a loop, not a 404") outright. The fix reuses existing, already-tested infrastructure: `buildAuthSignInHref`, `isSafeReturnPath`, and the single-use `storePostSignInReturnUrl` / `consumePostSignInReturnUrl` pair (already wired through `/auth/signin` and `CallbackClient.tsx`; 49/49 related Vitest assertions passed in the assessment session).

**Approach:**

1. In `archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorRoleGate.tsx`, replace the unconditional `router.replace("/welcome")` (JWT mode, no session) with `router.replace(buildAuthSignInHref({ returnPath: pathname + window.location.search }))`, imported from `@/lib/navigation/auth-sign-in-href`. Fall back to plain `/auth/signin` only when `isSafeReturnPath` rejects the path.
2. Leave `OperatorHomeGate.tsx` (`/` → `/welcome`) unchanged — the bare origin remaining the marketing landing for unsigned visitors is intentional; this ticket is scoped to non-home operator routes only.
3. Do not modify the PKCE/state/nonce logic in `initiate-redirect.ts` or `CallbackClient.tsx` — return-URL consumption on successful callback already works.

**Acceptance:**

- Unsigned JWT-mode visit to `/reviews/abc?x=1` redirects to `/auth/signin?returnUrl=%2Freviews%2Fabc%3Fx%3D1`, not `/welcome`.
- Unsafe/unparseable pathnames fall back to plain `/auth/signin` (no crash, no open redirect).
- Exempt routes (`/403`, `/auth/*`) and DevelopmentBypass mode are unaffected.
- After the IdP round-trip, the browser lands back on the originally requested path.

**Affected files:** `archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorRoleGate.tsx`, `archlucid-ui/src/components/OperatorRoleGate.test.tsx`.

**Depends on:** none.

**Size estimate:** S.

## TB-797 — Private-beta access-path canonical smoke test (P0)

**Window:** V1 (private beta).

**Status:** Done (2026-07-15) — `archlucid-ui/e2e/live-api-private-beta-access.spec.ts` + `e2e/helpers/live-private-beta-access.ts`; CI job **`ui-e2e-live-beta-access`** (JwtBearer build + scope-claim mint); documents JWT sessionStorage injection as CI stand-in for IdP OIDC; validates TB-796 deep-link `returnUrl` round-trip.

**Source:** Private-beta access-path assessment (2026-07-15) §10 — the required release gate before any beta invite is sent.

**Problem:** No automated test proves the full private-beta access path — invite/provision → real IdP sign-in → correct tenant → first action → session-expiry recovery → signed-out deep-link — under a beta auth mode (**JwtBearer**). Existing UI journey specs (e.g. `live-api-core-pilot-path.spec.ts`) run under **DevelopmentBypass**, which is not representative.

**Approach:**

1. Add `archlucid-ui/e2e/live-api-private-beta-access.spec.ts`, run under **JwtBearer** using the local-signing-key setup (`docs/library/LIVE_E2E_JWT_SETUP.md`, `scripts/ci/mint_ci_jwt.py`) — never DevelopmentBypass:
   1. Provision a fresh user via **TB-793**'s invite endpoint (or SCIM as interim if invite has not yet merged).

   3. Assert `/me` scope resolves to the expected tenant/workspace.

   5. Clear session-storage token keys to force expiry; recover via `/auth/session-expired`; confirm the review is still reachable.
   6. From a fresh signed-out browser context, deep-link the review URL and confirm it round-trips through sign-in back to the review (validates **TB-796**).
2. Add a dedicated CI job (e.g. `ui-e2e-live-beta-access`) gating any private-beta invite wave; do not fold into the existing DevBypass release-gate job.

**Acceptance:**

- Spec passes end to end under JwtBearer.
- CI job is documented as the required gate before sending beta invites.

**Depends on:** **TB-793**, **TB-794**, **TB-796** (benefits from **TB-795**'s invite test infrastructure).

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-925 — Fail closed on forged scope headers (private-beta access-path P0)

**Window:** V1 (private beta).

**Status:** **Done** (2026-07-22) — reconciled live observation vs source: JwtBearer + `AllowTestActorHeaders=false` DevBypass already enforce `ScopeIdentityBindingMiddleware` 403; added integration tests for `GET /v1/scope` and `GET /v1/admin/users/invitations`; `live-api-private-beta-access.spec.ts` TB-925 JwtBearer probe; documented DevBypass header-baking dev-only posture in `LIVE_E2E_JWT_SETUP.md`.

**Source:** Private-beta access-path assessment (2026-07-21), confirmed P0-1 (blocks proof 5 — tenant/workspace isolation). Ephemeral report: `docs/assessments/latest_beta_access_202607211939.md` (gitignored `latest_*.md`).

**Problem:** Against live local API `http://127.0.0.1:5128` (DevelopmentBypass, healthy), an authenticated principal with `tenant_id=11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111` still had effective scope steered by forged `x-tenant-id`:

1. `GET /api/auth/me` includes the default tenant/workspace/project claims.
2. `GET /v1/scope` with matching headers → default tenant.
3. `GET /v1/scope` with `x-tenant-id=bbbbbbbb-bbbb-bbbb-bbbb-bbbbbbbbbbbb` → **200** and `tenantId=bbbbbbbb-…` (forged).
4. `GET /v1/admin/users/invitations`: matching headers → **2** invites; forged tenant header → **0** invites (scope switched; not 403).
5. `GET /v1/authority/projects/default/runs?take=1` with forged tenant → **200** (not 403).

Current source documents the opposite: `HttpScopeContextProvider` claims win over headers; `ScopeIdentityBindingMiddleware` should 403 on claim/header mismatch; `ScopeIdentityBindingIntegrationTests` (DevBypass + Jwt variants) assert 403. Likely stale API process vs HEAD, or binding not effective on that host — treat as release-blocking until the **live host** passes the JwtBearer probe.

**Auth-mode matrix:** Must pass under **JwtBearer** (beta). Also verify **ApiKey** (existing integration tests). DevelopmentBypass must not ship to beta (`AuthSafetyGuard`).

**Cursor implementation prompt:**

```text
## Task
Private-beta access-path P0: prove tenant scope cannot be steered by forged x-tenant-id / x-workspace-id / x-project-id when the principal already carries scope claims. Current live API at 127.0.0.1:5128 was observed returning forged tenant from GET /v1/scope and changing GET /v1/admin/users/invitations results (HTTP 200, not 403). Current source claims claims-win + ScopeIdentityBindingMiddleware — reconcile process vs source.

## Constraints
- Do not weaken AuthSafetyGuard (DevelopmentBypass must remain blocked outside Development).
- Do not change marketing /welcome behavior except if required for operator deep links (TB-796 already routes unsigned operator routes via OperatorRoleGate → /auth/signin?returnUrl=).
- Keep each class in its own file; prefer concrete types; null-check; blank line before if/foreach when not first line.
- No ConfigureAwait(false) in tests.

## Likely files
- ArchLucid.Host.Core/Auth/Services/HttpScopeContextProvider.cs
- ArchLucid.Api/Middleware/ScopeIdentityBindingMiddleware.cs
- ArchLucid.Host.Core/Auth/Services/ScopeIdentityBindingValidator.cs
- ArchLucid.Api/Startup/PipelineExtensions.cs (middleware order: UseAuthentication → ScopeIdentityBinding → …)
- ArchLucid.Api.Tests/Security/ScopeIdentityBindingIntegrationTests.cs
- archlucid-ui/e2e/live-api-private-beta-access.spec.ts (or new live-api-scope-binding.spec.ts)
- archlucid-ui/src/lib/proxy-scope-resolution.ts (production must not forward attacker client scope)

## Acceptance criteria
1. Rebuild and restart ArchLucid.Api from current HEAD; re-run probe:
   - Principal with tenant_id claim + forged x-tenant-id → GET /v1/scope must NOT return forged tenant (claims win).
   - Same request → HTTP 403 from ScopeIdentityBindingMiddleware (or documented equivalent fail-closed).
2. Under JwtBearer (mint_ci_jwt.py + LIVE_JWT_TOKEN): same probe passes.
3. Under ApiKey with bound tenant claim: mismatch still 403 (existing tests stay green).
4. Add/extend live Playwright or API helper assertion in private-beta access suite so CI catches regression.
5. Document in LIVE_E2E_JWT_SETUP / happy-path note that beta gate requires this probe.

## Out of scope
- Visual/copy changes; SCIM UX; full pen test; GTM cohort work.

## Verify
- dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~ScopeIdentityBindingIntegrationTests
- Live HTTP probes above under JwtBearer
- npx playwright test live-api-private-beta-access.spec.ts (or new scope spec) with LIVE_JWT_TOKEN set
```

**Acceptance:** Same as prompt acceptance criteria 1–5.

**Depends on:** none (complements **TB-797**; prior invite/deep-link work **TB-793**–**TB-796** is Done).

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-723 ΓÇö Build-time static PDF generation pipeline (P1)

**Window:** V1.

**Status:** **Done** (2026-07-10) ΓÇö `ProductDocumentationPdfBuilder` + `archlucid docs pdf render`; `archlucid-ui/scripts/build-docs-pdf.ts` generates public PDFs under `public/docs-pdf/`, customer PDFs under `.build/docs-pdf-customer/`, and `public/docs-pdf/manifest.json`; `npm run build` invokes `build:docs-pdf` after `build:help-index`.

**Why:** The recommended Phase 1 architecture from `PDF_DOCUMENTATION_STRATEGY.md` ┬º2: generate PDFs once per deploy from the same markdown the live page renders, instead of a request-time render (rejected ΓÇö no per-viewer personalization needed) or a hand-committed binary (rejected ΓÇö drift risk).

**Approach:**

1. Add a CLI entry point to `Archlucid.Application/Pilots/MarkdownPdfRenderer.cs` (or a thin sibling) accepting a markdown path plus metadata JSON (title, version/date, audience, status), reusing the existing QuestPDF rendering rules ΓÇö no second markdownΓåÆPDF renderer.
2. Add a Node build script (family: `generate-brand-raster.mjs`, `build-help-search-index.mjs`) that iterates every `pdfStatus`-eligible registry entry, resolves its markdown via `tryLoadProductDocumentation`, derives the version date via `git log -1 --format=%cd -- {path}`, and invokes the CLI.
3. Public-status output ΓåÆ `archlucid-ui/public/docs-pdf/{slug}.pdf`. Customer-status output ΓåÆ a non-public build directory (consumed by **TB-726**). Internal-status entries are never generated.
4. Wire the script into the existing `build` pipeline (after `build:help-index`, before `next build`) and write `docs-pdf/manifest.json` (`{ slug, sourceSha256, generatedAt }`).

**Acceptance:**

- Every `pdfStatus: "public"` doc has a corresponding `public/docs-pdf/{slug}.pdf` after `npm run build`.
- No `pdfStatus: "internal"` doc ever produces a PDF artifact.
- Manifest hash matches current source markdown after every build.

**Affected files:** `Archlucid.Application/Pilots/MarkdownPdfRenderer.cs`, new `archlucid-ui/scripts/build-docs-pdf.mjs`, `archlucid-ui/package.json` (`build` script), `archlucid-ui/src/lib/load-product-documentation.ts`.

**Refs:** **TB-722**, **TB-724**, **TB-725**; existing pattern `archlucid-ui/scripts/generate-brand-raster.mjs`.

**Acceptance:**

- Met — settings repository binds tenant-scoped SQL factory; regression test fails if background-worker factory returns; docs describe the failure mode.

**Affected files:** `SqlTenantItsmOutboundSettingsRepository.cs`, `SqlTenantItsmOutboundSettingsRepositoryConnectionFactoryContractTests.cs`, `docs/runbooks/COMMON_ERRORS.md`, `docs/library/PRODUCTION_DEFECT_LOG.md` (**PD-002**).

## TB-868 — Eliminate stale frontend/CDN app shell after successful CD (P1)

**Window:** V1.

**Status:** **Done** (2026-07-17) — `next.config.ts` document-shell `no-store` with immutable `/_next/static` + `/images` override order; root layout `archlucid:build-commit` meta (`build-identity-html-meta.ts`); required CD smoke `ui_public_shell_build_id` (cache-bypass `/welcome`); [`FRONTEND_SHELL_CACHE.md`](../operations/FRONTEND_SHELL_CACHE.md) + Front Door honor-origin section in `infra/terraform-edge/README.md`.

**Problem:** CD can succeed while browsers/CDN continue serving an older frontend **application shell**. Operators then see a green deploy with stale UI.

**Already shipped (do not redo):**
- Next.js content-hashed `/_next/static` assets with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` in `archlucid-ui/next.config.ts` (production only).
- Standalone UI image + ACA revisions; `BUILD_ID` → `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_COMMIT_SHA` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_TIMESTAMP` in CD.
- Post-deploy product smoke compares API `/version` (+ UI health) `commitSha` to `BUILD_ID`.
- No service worker in `archlucid-ui` (re-verify when closing).

**Remaining scope:**
1. Ensure HTML / application bootstrap is **not** cached indefinitely (short TTL or `no-store`/`must-revalidate` as appropriate).
2. Audit Azure Front Door / CDN behavior; purge or invalidate **only** where required for version-sensitive entry content.
3. Add a post-deploy check that fetches a **public page** with cache-bypass headers and asserts the expected build ID.
4. Document expected cache propagation (immutable hashed assets vs version-sensitive shell).
5. Preserve safe long caching for immutable assets — do **not** blanket-disable caching; do **not** redesign the frontend.

**Acceptance:**
- After green CD, cache-bypass fetch of a public page shows the expected build identity.
- Docs explain how immutable assets differ from shell/HTML caching.
- Front Door/CDN purge is selective or justified as unnecessary.

**Size estimate:** M.

**Cross-ref:** **TB-754**–**TB-759** (cold-start / smoke), [`DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md`](DEPLOYMENT_CD_PIPELINE.md), `scripts/ci/cd_post_deploy_product_smoke.py`.

## TB-869 — Model alias & capability registry (P1) — **Done** (2026-07-18)

**Shipped:** `ArchLucid.Core/Agents/*` alias contracts; `ArchLucid.AgentRuntime/AgentModelAliases/*` config registry + resolver + router ambient binding; `AgentExecutionTrace.ModelAlias` + recorder propagation; DI in `RegisterAgentModelTierOrchestration`; unit/drift tests in `ArchLucid.AgentRuntime.Tests`.

**Window:** V1.1 — foundation for the AI model chooser; no provider change.

**Why:** Prompts, policies, config, and any future UI must not couple to literal Azure OpenAI deployment names. [`ai_model_chooser_plan_review_2026_07_18.md`](../architecture/ai_model_chooser_plan_review_2026_07_18.md) found tier→deployment mapping (`AgentModelTierOptions`) and a fine-tuned model registry already exist, but no customer-facing alias identity with capability tags and approved-task lists. ADR 0060 D2 makes aliases the only customer-visible model identity.

**Approach:**

1. Registry entity: alias (e.g. `economy-general`, `high-assurance-review`), provider connection kind, deployment name, capability tags (`structured-output`, `long-context`, `tool-use`, `advanced-reasoning`, …), approved task types.
2. Resolve alias → deployment inside the existing router path (`TieredAgentCompletionRouter` / `IAgentCompletionDeploymentResolver`); application services keep injecting `IAgentCompletionClient` unchanged.
3. Record alias (alongside existing deployment name) on `AgentExecutionTrace`.
4. Seed registry from current Economy/Standard/Premium tier deployments; config-only, no SQL required for the seed.

**Acceptance:**

- No literal deployment name in prompts, policy packs, or UI code paths; drift test guards the seed registry.
- Every live execution trace carries the resolved alias.
- Alias/task approval check fails closed: an unapproved alias/task pair is rejected before dispatch.

**Affected files:** `ArchLucid.Core` (registry contracts), `ArchLucid.AgentRuntime` (resolution), `AgentExecutionTrace.cs` + trace recorder, `AgentModelTierOptions.cs`, composition in `ServiceCollectionExtensions.AgentsGovernanceRetrieval.cs`.

**Refs:** ADR 0060 (D2), **TB-179** (tier routing), **TB-594** (fine-tuned registry pattern), **TB-870**.

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-870 — Workspace model-governance policy: default profile + per-review override (P1) — **Done** (2026-07-18)

**Window:** V1.1 — the "small chooser" slice; ArchLucid-managed provider only.

**Shipped:** `AgentModelExecutionProfile` + tier policy; tenant setting `ModelGovernance.DefaultExecutionProfile`; `IWorkspaceModelExecutionProfileService` + `IModelExecutionProfileResolver`; admin `GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/admin/settings/model-execution-profile`; optional `ArchitectureRequest.ModelExecutionProfileOverride` resolved at run create (fail closed on invalid); `RunStarterTaskFactory` applies profile to `ModelTierOverride`; audit `Workspace.ModelExecutionProfileUpdated`, `Workspace.ModelExecutionProfileOverrideCleared`, `Run.ModelExecutionProfileOverrideApplied`; tests in `ModelExecutionProfileResolverTests`, `WorkspaceModelExecutionProfileServiceTests`, `RunStarterTaskFactoryTierTests`, `SettingsControllerModelExecutionProfileTests`.

- Profile selection changes the resolved alias on subsequent execution traces; override applies to that review only.

## TB-872 — Customer-provided Azure OpenAI connection (first BYO path) (P2)

**Window:** V1.1 — ADR 0060 Accepted (2026-07-18); ADR-acceptance gate **cleared**. Do not start until **TB-869**–**TB-871** foundations land (or land in the same sequenced PR train).

**Why:** Highest-value BYO ask (customer tenancy, customer spend) with the least new code: reuses the existing `AzureOpenAiCompletionClient` shape with per-tenant client resolution, stays inside the ADR 0020 Azure-primary posture, and needs no new vendor SDK.

**Approach:**

1. Per-tenant AI provider connection entity (endpoint, deployment(s), auth mode); secret material via `ISecretProvider` / `IIntegrationSecretWriter` (Key Vault) — never ordinary config or DB columns (mirror **TB-392** per-tenant ITSM credential pattern).
2. Per-tenant `AzureOpenAIClient` resolution in the decorator pipeline; connection health probe + circuit-breaking scoped to the connection.
3. Provenance: provider connection ID on `AgentExecutionTrace`.
4. Metering per ADR 0060 D6: token usage + cost estimate recorded; wallet settlement and ArchLucid dollar-budget enforcement skipped; optional workspace quota.
5. No silent fallback from a customer connection to ArchLucid-paid capacity; failures surface as errors unless the workspace opts in.
6. Embeddings remain ArchLucid-managed (ADR 0060 D5) — connection applies to completions only; UI copy states this.

**Acceptance:**

- ADR 0060 Accepted (met 2026-07-18).
- Credential round-trips only through the secret boundary; repository/API tests prove no plaintext persistence.
- Executions on a customer connection carry the connection ID in trace + audit; wallet is not charged.
- Connection failure degrades only that workspace, with operator-visible health state.

**Affected files:** new connection entity + repository (`ArchLucid.Persistence`), secret wiring (`ServiceCollectionExtensions.TenancyMeteringSecrets.cs`), per-tenant client resolution (`ScopedInnerAgentCompletionClient` area), `LlmCompletionAccountingClient` (D6 branch), admin UI extension of **TB-871**.

**Refs:** ADR 0060 (D3, D5, D6), ADR 0020, **TB-080** (MI auth), **TB-392** (per-tenant credential pattern), **TB-869**–**TB-871**.

**Size estimate:** L.

## TB-873 — Generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint adapter (second BYO path) (P3)

**Window:** V2 — **GATED (ADR 0060 D4 remaining): (b) structured-output capability probe passes for the target endpoint or an approved degraded-parsing profile exists; (c) per-alias faithfulness-harness pass artifact before any task is approvable on that alias.** Gate (a) ADR 0060 Accepted — **met** 2026-07-18. Go-path of closed **TB-689**.

**Why:** One adapter covers many customer-hosted providers (open-weight servers, LiteLLM-style gateways) without N vendor SDKs. Deliberately last: "OpenAI-compatible" endpoints vary on JSON-schema structured output, which agent code paths depend on (`UseJsonSchemaResponseFormat`), and hosted third-party endpoints receiving regulated customer evidence change the data-boundary story.

**Approach:**

1. `OpenAiCompatibleCompletionClient` implementing `IAgentCompletionClient` against the OpenAI HTTP surface; connection entity + secrets reuse **TB-872** infrastructure.
2. Capability probe on connection setup: strict JSON-schema support, context length, token-usage reporting; probe result stored on the connection and rechecked on failure patterns.
3. Eval gate: alias/task approval in the **TB-869** registry requires a faithfulness-harness pass artifact (offline golden floors; Phase B where applicable) for that alias; approval fails closed without it.
4. Hosted third-party endpoints: workspace-admin regulated-evidence acknowledgment recorded in the audit trail before first use (ADR 0060 D4).
5. Content safety and all deterministic authority behaviors run unchanged on this path (ADR 0060 D7).

**Acceptance:**

- Remaining gates evidenced in the PR (probe artifact, eval pass artifact); ADR 0060 Accepted already on file.
- Endpoint failing the structured-output probe cannot be approved for schema-dependent tasks.
- Trace/audit parity with Azure paths: alias, connection ID, token usage, cost estimate, fallback attempts.
- **TB-689** already closed with pointer to this item + ADR 0060.

**Affected files:** new adapter in `ArchLucid.AgentRuntime`, `DefaultLlmProviderFactory.cs` (`LlmProviderType` activation), capability-probe service, registry approval gate (**TB-869**), audit acknowledgment event, admin UI extension.

**Refs:** ADR 0060 (D4, D7), **TB-689**, **TB-869**, **TB-872**, faithfulness harness (**TB-683**, `eval_agent_faithfulness.py`).

**Size estimate:** XL.

4. Persistence + audit + citation parity with Azure extractor; trust-center / help copy: Tier 1 default = no ArchLucid credentials in customer AWS/GCP.

**Acceptance:**

- Does **not** implement **TB-214** (arbitrary non-extractor evidence JSON).

**Affected files:** `scripts/Get-ArchLucidAwsPackage*`, `scripts/Get-ArchLucidGcpPackage*`, Core extractor readers, API upload controllers, OpenAPI snapshot + `ArchLucid.Api.Client`, help/trust copy (`/help/cloud-connections/{aws,gcp}` extensions), operator upload UI if missing for Aws/Gcp Tier 1.

## TB-877 — Community summarization Graph-RAG (RAG-V2-001 remainder) (P1)

**Window:** V1 — owner overrode [ADR 0057](../architecture/adrs/0057-graph-rag-community-summarization-scope-decision.md) option (b) deferral on 2026-07-05 in favor of option (a) (implement now). Accepts unproven live-model quality risk until a dedicated ablation lands.

**Why:** Bounded multi-hop (**TB-597**) only reaches 1–2 hops. Community-level thematic summaries deepen Graph-RAG differentiability for cross-node themes that neighbor expansion cannot surface. Scope was previously "assign TB at implement"; this row is that TB.

**Defaults (owner-approved via "do it" 2026-07-19 unless later overridden):**

- Detection algorithm: **Leiden** preferred; Louvain acceptable if dependency/licensing is simpler.
- Feature **default off** (config flag); no buyer-facing "community Graph-RAG shipped" claim until quality evidence exists.
- Retrieval-only integration first (inject community summaries into retrieval context); no new operator UI required for V1 slice.

**Approach:**

1. Community-detection pass over existing `GraphSnapshot` (respect `FullGraphResponseMaxNodes` / bounded graph).
2. One hierarchical LLM summarization call per detected community; route spend through `LlmMonthlyTenantDollarBudgetTracker`.
3. Cache + re-embed on ADR 0004 outbox refresh cadence (reuse `AzureOpenAiEmbeddingService` / `AzureAiSearchVectorIndex` per ADR 0036 — no new vector subprocessor).
4. Exclude derived community-summary artifacts from `GraphSnapshotCanonicalFingerprint`.
5. Wire into retrieval when Graph-RAG advanced retrieval is enabled **and** the community-summarization flag is on; inherit `GraphRagProductionLikeConfigurationLint` posture honesty (unproven without production vector index).
6. Add offline golden-cohort ablation path (TB-595 methodology) as a follow-on acceptance stretch or immediate sibling test artifact — do not claim production quality without it.

**Acceptance:**

- With flag on, a graph with multiple communities produces cached summaries that retrieval can cite; with flag off, behavior matches today's bounded multi-hop only.
- Summaries never alter `GraphSnapshotCanonicalFingerprint`.
- Tenant budget tracker records summarization spend; failure/degrade paths are scoped to that tenant.
- Unit tests for detection + cache invalidation on graph change; no buyer docs claim proven quality.
- Cross-link this ID from ADR 0057 addendum and `V1_SCOPE.md` §2.20 / `V1_DEFERRED.md` §6q.

**Affected files:** Graph-RAG / retrieval packages (`GraphRagNeighborExpander` area, new community detector + summarizer services), outbox indexing path, `Retrieval:Advanced` options, golden-cohort / ablation fixtures, config lint copy if needed.

**Refs:** ADR 0057 (option (a) addendum), ADR 0036, ADR 0004, **TB-595**, **TB-596**, **TB-597**, [`V1_SCOPE.md`](V1_SCOPE.md) §2.20, [`V1_DEFERRED.md`](V1_DEFERRED.md) §6q.

**Size estimate:** L.

## TB-878 — Iterative retrieve-critique-retry loop (RAG-V2-002 remainder) (P2)

**Window:** V1 — owner promoted from validation-first hold (`LATEST_GPT55.md` §17 Promoted to V1); overrides TB-598 deferral pending G-REAL-06.

**Why:** Single-pass query expansion (**TB-598**) ships one LLM rewrite + one HyDE + semantic rerank. The promoted remainder adds **bounded multi-round** retrieval: after each round, a critique step judges whether evidence is sufficient to answer the query intent; if not, emit a refined query and retrieve again — without relabeling today's single-pass path as "agentic retrieval."

**Defaults:**

- Feature **default off** (`Retrieval:Advanced:EnableIterativeRetrieveCritiqueRetry` or equivalent).
- Max rounds configurable (default **2**, hard cap **3**).
- Fail-open to last-good chunk set on budget/timeout; record rounds in grounding trace.

**Approach:**

1. Add critique + re-query orchestration inside advanced retrieval (`AgenticRetrievalCompletionClient` / `RetrievalQueryService` area) after initial single-pass expansion.
2. Critique prompt returns structured verdict: `sufficient` | `requery` + optional refined query text; no unbounded agent loop.
3. Extend **TB-595** ablation profiles with iterative-loop on/off; add golden fixture where multi-round improves recall without faithfulness regression.
4. Buyer-facing docs stay on **single-pass query expansion** unless/until live-model evidence exists.

**Acceptance:**

- Flag off: identical behavior to current single-pass expansion + rerank.
- Flag on: at least one golden fixture shows higher recall@k vs single-pass; faithfulness cohort floors unchanged.
- Grounding trace records round count + critique decisions; tenant budget tracker accounts for extra LLM calls.
- Cross-link **TB-878** from `V1_SCOPE.md` §2.20 and `V1_DEFERRED.md` §6q (iterative remainder).

**Affected files:** `ArchLucid.Retrieval` advanced retrieval orchestration, retrieval options, golden-cohort/ablation fixtures, config lint copy if needed.

**Refs:** **TB-598**, **TB-595**, `AgenticRetrievalCompletionClient`, [`V1_MAGIC_GUARDRAILS.md`](V1_MAGIC_GUARDRAILS.md).

**Size estimate:** L.

**Acceptance:**

- Materialize with retrieval enabled links at least one cited pilot signal on a fixture opportunity cluster.
- Tenant isolation tests prove no cross-tenant retrieval at upsert or query time.
- No mutation of agents, prompts, or policy packs from pilot-feedback retrieval.
- OpenAPI + generated clients updated if DTO fields added.

**Affected files:** `ProductLearningPlanningDerivationService`, retrieval indexing for pilot signals, `LearningController`, `PlanningBridgePanel`, `PRODUCT_LEARNING.md` §4.

**Closure:** `archlucid-ui/src/lib/showcase-page-resolution.ts` + tests; `(marketing)/showcase/[runId]/page.tsx` serves curated static without upstream fetch for `claims-intake-modernization` and falls back on marketing API **404**/**invalid**; `e2e/showcase-static-first.spec.ts`; `docs/library/DEMO_PREVIEW.md` deploy posture for `SHOWCASE_STATIC_ONLY`.

Reachable API → **404** → `DemoPreviewNotAvailable` with **no** static fallback — worse than API-down path. Mock E2E masks this via `SHOWCASE_STATIC_ONLY=1` and mock API 200 for any slug.

**Approach:**
