## TB-961 — Worker SIGTERM / scale-in graceful drain + execute ownership release (P1)

**Window:** V1 — Reliability.

**Status:** Not started.

**Priority:** P1.

**Source:** ACA Worker failure semantics 2026-07-23 (PA Q16).

**Problem:** Hard kill / scale-in can leave execute ownership held until lease timeout while another replica cannot safely resume; or two replicas race. Outbox already has `LockedUntilUtc`; execute path needs the same **drain story** on `IHostApplicationLifetime` / ACA termination grace.

**Approach:**

1. On SIGTERM / stopping token: stop dequeuing new pipeline/execute work; finish or cooperatively abort current agent call within grace; persist any completed `AgentResult` before exit.
2. Release or shorten execute ownership lease / heartbeat so peer can claim after grace (coordinate with **TB-943** lease design — implement host half here if **TB-943** not yet landed, or merge PR).
3. Terraform/docs: Worker `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (or ACA equivalent) sized above longest expected cooperative abort + SQL write.
4. Metrics: `worker_drain_started`, `worker_drain_forced_kill`, lease-release latency.
5. Tests: stopping-token fixture asserts no new claim after drain start; lease free within grace.

**Acceptance:** Documented grace + code path; peer resume after drain does not double-run tasks already persisted (**TB-039**); ops note in **TB-960** contract.

**Depends on:** **TB-960** (contract). Implements/hosts **TB-943**. Benefits from **TB-937** status vocabulary.

**Out of scope:** Changing KEDA/queue scale rules (**TB-915**); raising `min_replicas` for availability.

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-967 — Bounded webhook body intake (size before HMAC) (P1)

**Window:** V1 — Trustworthiness.

**Status:** Not started.

**Priority:** P1.

**Source:** Hostile-internet webhook gap 2026-07-23 (PA Q3).

**Problem:** Size checks after full `ReadToEndAsync` still allocate the attack body; missing/lying `Content-Length` and chunked bombs bypass naive caps. Signature verify on unbounded buffers is CPU DoS.

**Approach:**

1. Shared helper: reject when `Content-Length` > max; stream/read with hard byte ceiling; return 413/400 before HMAC/parse.
2. Apply to ITSM inbound, Stripe webhook, Marketplace webhook (and any other `[AllowAnonymous]` inbound body consumers).
3. Keep verify on **raw bounded bytes** before `JsonDocument.Parse`; Content-Type allowlist where vendor-fixed.
4. Architecture + integration tests: oversized body never reaches parse/verify crypto path; constant-time compare retained.
5. Metrics/audit: payload-too-large counts without storing body.

**Acceptance:** All inbound webhook controllers use bounded intake; tests lock size-before-verify-before-parse; **TB-966** inventory rows updated.

**Depends on:** **TB-966**. Extends existing `MaxInboundWebhookPayloadUtf8Bytes` / billing buffering patterns.

**Out of scope:** Changing vendor signature algorithms; raising global API body limits for authenticated routes.

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-976 — Durable per-reservation leases + orphan reclaim + paid-unsettle reconcile (P1)

**Window:** V1 — Cost-effectiveness.

**Status:** Not started.

**Priority:** P1.

**Source:** Follow-on to **TB-975** — replica crash between reserve and settle.

**Problem:** Crash after reserve leaves `ReservedAssumedUsd` stuck (false hard-stop). Crash after successful provider call before settle under-counts `SpentUsd` while still holding reserved. `ReleasePendingReservationIfAnyAsync` only runs on a live request path.

**Approach:**

1. Introduce durable reservation rows (or equivalent): `ReservationId`, tenant, period, reserved USD, `ExpiresUtc`, state (Reserved/Settled/Released/Expired).
2. Reserve/settle/release by id (pattern from Quick Scan **TB-894**); keep monthly roll-up for cap checks.
3. Background/orphan reclaim: expire stale Reserved → release pressure; alert on reclaim rate.
4. Paid-unsettle reconcile: when usage/trace proves tokens were consumed without settle, commit actual (or conservative estimate) and clear reservation — document residual windows.
5. Tests: kill replica after reserve (no call) → reclaim restores headroom; kill after success before settle → reconcile increases Spent without double-count.

**Acceptance:** No unbounded orphan reserved pool in staging kill drill; reconcile path documented; dual-replica tests extended beyond Done **TB-011** happy-path concurrency.

**Depends on:** **TB-975**. Reuses **TB-894** ideas; complements **TB-939** (batch admit) without replacing per-call leases.

**Out of scope:** Exactly-once Azure OpenAI billing; rewriting wallet ledger.

**Size estimate:** L.

## TB-977 — SQL-owned UTC period key + reserved-pool admission fairness (P1)

**Window:** V1 — Reliability.

**Status:** Not started.

**Priority:** P1.

**Source:** Follow-on to **TB-975** — clock skew at month boundary; tenant racing assumed-max reserves.

**Problem:** App `TimeProvider` month keys can split one UTC month across two ledger rows near rollover. Racing N concurrent calls each reserving assumed-max fills the reserved pool (soft-DoS) without bypassing the hard cap.

**Approach:**

1. Decide period membership inside reserve/settle SQL (or single trusted clock at repository boundary) using `SYSUTCDATETIME()`; reject or remap cross-period settle of a reservation minted in another period with explicit rules.
2. Admission fairness: per-tenant in-flight reservation count/USD ceiling and/or concurrency gate before reserve (cf. Quick Scan **TB-896**); optionally tighten assumed-max or use tighter estimates when headroom is low.
3. Metrics/alerts: reserved-pool saturation, optimistic-retry exhaustion, period-remap events.
4. Tests: skew two clocks across month boundary cannot exceed one intended monthly hard cap; race flood hits admission/429/quota rather than sticky false exhaustion without reclaim (**TB-976**).

**Acceptance:** Month-boundary integration test green; race suite documents cap-hold + fairness behavior; docs updated.

**Depends on:** **TB-975**; benefits from **TB-976** leases (period stamped on reservation). Pairs open **TB-939**.

**Out of scope:** Global anonymous Quick Scan budgets (already **TB-894**); changing hard-cap product amounts.

**Size estimate:** M.

## TB-986 — Finding concurrent disposition / HumanReviewStatus conflict contract (P1)

**Window:** V1 — Data consistency.

**Status:** Not started.

**Priority:** P1.

**Source:** Owner / PA question 2026-07-24: *If two operators race approve and reject on the same finding, what is the conflict rule and the durable outcome?*

**Problem:** Governance **approval requests** document and implement first-wins CAS (`TryTransitionFromReviewableAsync`, loser **409**). Finding **dispositions** and ITSM-driven **`HumanReviewStatus`** do not share that rule, but buyer/operator language (“approve” / “reject”) invites the false belief that finding finalize is mutually exclusive. No single PA-defensible contract states the finding conflict rule, durable outcome, and when (if ever) a mutex is required.

**Approach:**

1. Author `docs/library/FINDING_CONCURRENT_DISPOSITION_CONFLICT_CONTRACT.md` (or contributor-reference section under `GOVERNANCE.md` + `FINDINGS_OPERATOR_GUIDE.md`) with a decision table:
   - **Finding disposition trail:** append-only; racing writes **both persist**; **current** = latest `OccurredAtUtc` (inspect / stickiness history).
   - **`HumanReviewStatus` (ITSM inbound):** last-writer `UPDATE` on scoped `FindingRecords` row; no 409; may diverge from disposition trail unless mapped disposition also appends (**TB-396** Done path).
   - **Governance approval request Approve/Reject:** first successful transition wins; loser conflict — **out of finding scope** but must be contrasted so PA answers do not conflate the two.
   - **Owner choice for V1:** (A) keep append-only + document + UX honesty (**TB-987** default), or (B) introduce contradictory-disposition / terminal-status mutex (409) — record decision in the contract before **TB-987** codes it.
2. Cross-link `GOVERNANCE_WORKFLOW_UI.md`, `API_CONTRACTS.md` disposition endpoints, Done approval-request concurrent tests.
3. Name enforcement surfaces for **TB-987** and race fixtures for **TB-988**.

**Acceptance:** Contract published with explicit durable outcome for racing operators; GTM **M-140**/**M-141** can cite it; **TB-987** implements the chosen option without silently changing approval-request CAS.

**Depends on:** None (docs). Complements Done approval-request CAS / disposition trail / **TB-390**/**TB-396**.

**Out of scope:** Changing segregation-of-duties on approval requests; ITSM vendor workflow redesign (**TB-398** V2).

**Size estimate:** S.

## TB-987 — Enforce finding race honesty (stale UX + status alignment) (P1)

**Window:** V1 — Correctness.

**Status:** Not started.

**Priority:** P1.

**Source:** Follow-on to **TB-986**.

**Problem:**

1. `FindingInspectGovernanceStickinessPanel` / disposition save can succeed while another operator’s newer disposition already exists — UI may keep showing a stale “current” until manual refresh.
2. `FindingReviewAction.Approve` / `Reject` exist on the trail mapper but operator path is disposition-centric; `HumanReviewStatus` Approved/Rejected from ITSM can overwrite without surfacing conflict to operators watching the finding.
3. If **TB-986** chooses option (B), there is no server-side contradictory-disposition guard today (both inserts always succeed).

**Approach:**

1. Per **TB-986** option (A) default: after save, re-fetch latest disposition; if another event is newer than the client’s baseline, show explicit concurrent-update copy (“Another operator recorded {disposition} at {time} — current is that event”); keep full history visible.
2. If option (B): reject contradictory terminal dispositions with **409** ProblemDetails when a newer conflicting disposition exists within a documented window (or when expected `LatestDispositionOccurredAtUtc` precondition fails); document idempotency-key interaction.
3. Align inspect `HumanReviewStatus` display with trail/ITSM provenance (label source: operator disposition vs ITSM webhook); do not invent mutex on ITSM unless contract requires it.
4. Unit/API tests for stale-baseline and dual-writer happy paths.

**Acceptance:** Operator cannot silently believe a lost race “won”; behavior matches **TB-986** chosen option; approval-request 409 path unchanged.

**Depends on:** **TB-986**.

**Out of scope:** Bulk-disposition fan-out redesign; approval-queue UI; full bidirectional ITSM mapping (**TB-398**).

**Size estimate:** M.

**Problem:** Commit path, hash, and proof-language taxonomy exist, but PA/sales still lack one matrix that states: **committed golden manifest** (`dbo.GoldenManifests` / `GoldenManifestId` + `ManifestHash`) is the only unit of truth for review-backed “we finalized this” claims; exports are projections; uncommitted/intermediate/illustrative surfaces must not be sold as that record. Same gap for **chain hop-skips**: features that emit buyer claims without walking Evidence → Finding → **Commit** → Artifact → Audit, and for the **honest labels** to use instead of inventing a parallel “signed” story.

**Approach:**

1. Author `docs/library/COMMITTED_GOLDEN_MANIFEST_UNIT_OF_TRUTH_CONTRACT.md` (or expand `PUBLIC_CLAIM_BOUNDARY_GUIDE.md` + `PROOF_LANGUAGE_CLAIM_AUDIT.md`) with tables:
   - **Unit of truth:** committed golden manifest (buyer: finalized architecture package / signed review record).
   - **Chain hops (required for `review-backed`):** Evidence → Finding → Manifest (commit) → Artifact (projection) → Audit (append-only ledger).
   - **Projections (OK if labeled):** sponsor PDF/DOCX/ZIP export-verify — derived from commit, not a second authority.
   - **Forbidden substitutes / hop-skips:** uncommitted `Run` / ReadyForCommit / partial execute; findings snapshot alone; agent results/traces alone; `DraftRequests`; Ask/RAG answers; Simulator/demo/seed as customer outcome; UI executive summary / chat transcript; governance approval without commit; artifact-without-commit; “audit” that is UI logs only.
   - **Honest labels (instead of faking):** Ask/chat/explainer → **conversational** / assistive; uncommitted/draft → **draft** / in progress; findings before commit → **working findings**; Simulator/showcase → **illustrative sample** / demo-derived; sponsor export → **export / projection**; ROI on those surfaces → **estimate** / basis-labeled (coordinate **TB-983**–**TB-985**, do not duplicate dollar-forbid rules).
   - **Cross-links:** pre-commit gate, export verify (TB-307 / ADR 0040), `COMPLETE_REVIEW_WORKFLOW`, `PILOT_MISCONFIGURATION_GUARDS` (sponsor before commit); sealed evidence **TB-1009**; Required audit **TB-953**.
2. Explicit non-goals: renaming API `GoldenManifest`; changing seal triggers; Simulator ROI dollar rules (**TB-983**–**TB-985**); new TB/M IDs for the chain Q (owned here).
3. Name CI anchors for **TB-1004**; GTM **M-154**/**M-155**.

**Acceptance:** Contract published with unit-of-truth + hop/label matrices; GTM can cite it; does not claim WORM/PKI beyond application-layer hash lineage.

**Depends on:** None (docs). Builds on shipped commit/hash.

**Out of scope:** New persistence model; “Architecture” as separate top-level entity (object-model assessment); reopening **TB-1009**/**TB-953** implementation.

**Size estimate:** S.
